summary: Qwen3.5-0.8B gets stuck repeating lines that start with "Wait" and runs out of tokens: it solves 8.2% of MATH-500. We showed Inkling 2 Small one MLP layer of Qwen as a small table read from its weights, six tokens by 64 neurons, and wrote its answer into the real model. Scaling down how hard layer 23 pushes the two "Wait" tokens lifts MATH-500 to 38.2% [34.0, 42.4], level with the published one-neuron edit that was found with closed frontier models (+2.4 points [-3.6, +8.4] on the 250 problems both were run on). Proposers trained by RL on Tinker, on small networks only, give this kind of edit in one answer of about 137 tokens with no reasoning: 15 of their 16 answers for this layer helped, against 2 of 8 random edits. Untrained, Inkling 2 Small finds it too, by reasoning for about 1,685 tokens. When the same table is shown with its numbers shuffled, only 6 of 16 answers help, so the proposers are using the weights they read.
